subject: Mathematics

source.subtopic: Introduce formal measuring (ml, litre): know that 1 cup = 250 ml, teaspoon = 5 ml

show.line: A big bottle holds one litre. A cup holds 250 millilitres. A teaspoon holds just five millilitres!

rounds.praise: Yes! The bucket holds the most.

rounds.prompt: Which container holds about one litre?
rounds.praise: Yes! A big milk bottle is one litre.

rounds.prompt: Four cups fill the one litre jug. How many cups of 250 millilitres make a litre?
Would you measure medicine in millilitres or litres? Say it.
Millilitres or litres? Pick the unit for each.
Read the measuring jug. How much water is in it?
rounds.praise: Yes! 500 millilitres. That is half a litre.

hints: Millilitres for small amounts. Litres for big amounts.
A cup is 250 millilitres. Four cups make one litre.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will fill the litre jug with cups.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: One cup, two cups. Full! Two cups make a litre.
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Two cups is only 500 millilitres. Four cups make a litre.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's pour together. One, two, three, four cups. Now it is a litre!

parent_line: Can compare how much containers hold and knows cups, millilitres and litres.
